images.alt: Three brass rifle cartridges standing upright against a dark background. The left has a pink polymer-tipped bullet, the centre a plain copper open-tip bullet, and the right a longer, more sharply pointed copper bullet seated deeper in a shorter visible case.
images.caption: Three .300 AAC Blackout loads: a 125-grain polymer-tip hunting round, a 125-grain open-tip match round, and (right) a 220-grain subsonic round, whose heavier bullet is seated further down into the case.

images.alt: A black and white line drawing of a bottlenecked rifle cartridge in profile, dimensioned in inches: case and rim diameter .378, shoulder angle 23 degrees, neck diameter .334, case length to shoulder 1.071 and 1.102, and overall length 2.260 maximum.
images.caption: Dimensional diagram of the .300 AAC Blackout, showing the short 1.368-inch case built to headspace and feed from an unmodified 5.56x45mm/.223 Remington bolt and magazine.

images.alt: A rendered illustration of four rifle cartridges standing side by side: a short brass round with a dark bullet, a slightly taller round with a grey-green steel case, and two taller, slimmer brass rounds with pointed bullets.
images.caption: A rendered size comparison, left to right: .300 AAC Blackout, 7.62x39mm, 6.8mm Remington SPC, and 5.56x45mm NATO. The Blackout is built to match 5.56x45mm case-head dimensions and magazine length while carrying a bullet close in diameter to the 7.62x39mm.
